answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to a unique, costly proof-of-work atlas that must be solved once at registration and refreshed with every major action. The willow of cheap fakes withers because forging many identities demands repeated computational effort proportional to the number of heads. A shared prism of graded work history further multiplies the cost: attackers must also sustain original, peer-attested output across epochs or lose standing and rewards.
